ML-KEM.primary_use: Key establishment, general encryption key exchange, TLS 1.3 handshake

tradeoffs.performance: Extremely fast key generation, encapsulation, and decapsulation (sub-millisecond)
tradeoffs.overhead: Public key (1184 B) and ciphertext (1088 B) are significantly larger than X25519 (32 B) or RSA-2048 (256 B)
tradeoffs.mtu_impact: Fits within standard 1500 MTU for TLS ClientHello/ServerHello when bundled properly

ML-DSA.primary_use: General purpose digital signatures, certificates, authentication, code signing

tradeoffs.overhead: Signatures are 2.4 KB - 4.6 KB, compared to RSA-2048 (256 B) or ECDSA P-256 (64 B). Requires protocol buffer and MTU re-engineering.

SLH-DSA.primary_use: Conservative digital signatures, long-term trust roots, secure boot, backup if lattice assumptions face theoretical advances

tradeoffs.performance: Significantly slower signing time and very large signature sizes (8 KB - 30 KB)
tradeoffs.advantage: Rooted only in standard cryptographic hash functions (SHA-2/SHAKE), extremely conservative security assurance

HYBRID-KEM.formal_name: Composite / Dual Classical + Post-Quantum Key Exchange
HYBRID-KEM.primary_use: Transition phase TLS 1.3, SSH, VPNs (e.g., X25519 + ML-KEM-768)
HYBRID-KEM.advantage: Guarantees classical security even if lattice math is compromised, while protecting against SNDL today

AES-256.primary_use: Bulk symmetric encryption at rest and in transit
AES-256.advantage: Retains 128-bit quantum security against Grover's algorithm. Already standard and widely accelerated in hardware (AES-NI).
